auth:

  username: user
  ## @param auth.password RabbitMQ application password

  ##
  password: ""
  ## @param auth.securePassword Whether to set the RabbitMQ password securely. This is incompatible with loading external RabbitMQ definitions and 'true' when not setting the auth.password parameter.
  ## ref: https://github.com/bitnami/containers/tree/main/bitnami/rabbitmq#environment-variables
  ##
  securePassword: true
  ## @param auth.updatePassword Update RabbitMQ password on secret change
  ## ref: https://github.com/bitnami/containers/tree/main/bitnami/rabbitmq#environment-variables
  ##

  ## NOTE: ignored unless `auth.existingErlangSecret` parameter is set
  ##

  ## Enable encryption to rabbitmq

  ## @param auth.tls.enabled Enable TLS support on RabbitMQ
  ## @param auth.tls.autoGenerated Generate automatically self-signed TLS certificates
  ## @param auth.tls.failIfNoPeerCert When set to true, TLS connection will be rejected if client fails to provide a certificate
  ## @param auth.tls.sslOptionsVerify Should [peer verification](https://www.rabbitmq.com/ssl.html#peer-verification) be enabled?

    enabled: false
    autoGenerated: false
    failIfNoPeerCert: true

    sslOptionsPassword:

      existingSecret: ""
      key: ""
      password: ""
    caCertificate: ""
    serverCertificate: ""
    serverKey: ""
    existingSecret: ""
    existingSecretFullChain: false
    overrideCaCertificate: ""
## @param logs Path of the RabbitMQ server's Erlang log file. Value for the `RABBITMQ_LOGS` environment variable
## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/logging.html#log-file-location
##
logs: "-"

##

## ref: https://github.com/bitnami/charts/issues/2189
## @param maxAvailableSchedulers RabbitMQ maximum available scheduler threads
## @param onlineSchedulers RabbitMQ online scheduler threads
##
maxAvailableSchedulers: ""
onlineSchedulers: ""
## The memory threshold under which RabbitMQ will stop reading from client network sockets, in order to avoid being killed by the OS
## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/alarms.html
## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/memory.html#threshold
##
memoryHighWatermark:
  ## @param memoryHighWatermark.enabled Enable configuring Memory high watermark on RabbitMQ
  ##
  enabled: false
  ## @param memoryHighWatermark.type Memory high watermark type. Either `absolute` or `relative`
  ##
  type: "relative"
  ## Memory high watermark value.
  ## @param memoryHighWatermark.value Memory high watermark value
  ## The default value of 0.4 stands for 40% of available RAM
  ## Note: the memory relative limit is applied to the resourcesPreset memory limit or the resource.limits.memory to calculate the memory threshold
  ## You can also use an absolute value, e.g.: 256Mi
  ##
  value: 0.4
## @param plugins List of default plugins to enable (should only be altered to remove defaults; for additional plugins use `extraPlugins`)
##
plugins: "rabbitmq_management rabbitmq_peer_discovery_k8s"

## @param queue_leader_locator Changes the queue_leader_locator setting in the rabbitmq config file
##
queue_leader_locator: balanced
## @param queue_master_locator DEPRECATED.  Use queue_leader_locator instead
##
queue_master_locator: ""

## @param communityPlugins List of Community plugins (URLs) to be downloaded during container initialization
## Combine it with extraPlugins to also enable them.
##
communityPlugins: ""
## @param extraPlugins Extra plugins to enable (single string containing a space-separated list)
## Use this instead of `plugins` to add new plugins
##
extraPlugins: "rabbitmq_auth_backend_ldap"
## Clustering settings
##
clustering:
  ## @param clustering.enabled Enable RabbitMQ clustering
  ##
  enabled: true
  ## @param clustering.name RabbitMQ cluster name
  ## If not set, a name is generated using the common.names.fullname template
  ##
  name: ""
  ## @param clustering.addressType Switch clustering mode. Either `ip` or `hostname`
  ##
  addressType: hostname
  ## @param clustering.rebalance Rebalance master for queues in cluster when new replica is created
  ## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/rabbitmq-queues.8.html#rebalance
  ##
  rebalance: false
  ## @param clustering.forceBoot Force boot of an unexpectedly shut down cluster (in an unexpected order).
  ## forceBoot executes 'rabbitmqctl force_boot' to force boot cluster shut down unexpectedly in an unknown order
  ## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/rabbitmqctl.8.html#force_boot
  ##
  forceBoot: false
  ## @param clustering.partitionHandling Switch Partition Handling Strategy. Either `autoheal` or `pause_minority` or `pause_if_all_down` or `ignore`
  ## ref: https://www.rabbitmq.com/partitions.html#automatic-handling
  ##
  partitionHandling: autoheal
## Loading a RabbitMQ definitions file to configure RabbitMQ
##
loadDefinition:
  ## @param loadDefinition.enabled Enable loading a RabbitMQ definitions file to configure RabbitMQ
  ##
  enabled: false
  ## @param loadDefinition.file Name of the definitions file
  ##
  file: "/app/load_definition.json"
  ## @param loadDefinition.existingSecret Existing secret with the load definitions file
  ## Can be templated if needed, e.g:
  ## existingSecret: "{{ .Release.Name }}-load-definition"
  ##
  existingSecret: ""
## @param command Override default container command (useful when using custom images)
##
command: []
## @param args Override default container args (useful when using custom images)
##
args: []
## @param lifecycleHooks Overwrite livecycle for the RabbitMQ container(s) to automate configuration before or after startup
##
lifecycleHooks: {}
## @param terminationGracePeriodSeconds Default duration in seconds k8s waits for container to exit before sending kill signal.
## Any time in excess of 10 seconds will be spent waiting for any synchronization necessary for cluster not to lose data.
##
terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120
## @param extraEnvVars Extra environment variables to add to RabbitMQ pods
## E.g:
## extraEnvVars:
##   - name: FOO
##     value: BAR
##
extraEnvVars: []
## @param extraEnvVarsCM Name of existing ConfigMap containing extra environment variables
##
extraEnvVarsCM: ""
## @param extraEnvVarsSecret Name of existing Secret containing extra environment variables (in case of sensitive data)
##
extraEnvVarsSecret: ""
## Container Ports
## @param containerPorts.amqp
## @param containerPorts.amqpTls
## @param containerPorts.dist
## @param containerPorts.manager
## @param containerPorts.epmd
## @param containerPorts.metrics
##
containerPorts:
  amqp: 5672
  amqpTls: 5671
  dist: 25672
  manager: 15672
  epmd: 4369
  metrics: 9419
## Host Ports
## @param hostPorts.amqp
## @param hostPorts.amqpTls
## @param hostPorts.manager
## @param hostPorts.metrics
##
hostPorts:
  amqp: ""
  amqpTls: ""
  manager: ""
  metrics: ""

## @param initScripts Dictionary of init scripts. Evaluated as a template.
## Specify dictionary of scripts to be run at first boot
## Alternatively, you can put your scripts under the files/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d directory
## For example:
## initScripts:
##   my_init_script.sh: |
##      #!/bin/sh
##      echo "Do something."
##
initScripts: {}
## @param initScriptsCM ConfigMap with the init scripts. Evaluated as a template.
## Note: This will override initScripts
##
initScriptsCM: ""
## @param initScriptsSecret Secret containing `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` scripts to be executed at initialization time that contain sensitive data. Evaluated as a template.
##
initScriptsSecret: ""
## @param extraContainerPorts Extra ports to be included in container spec, primarily informational
## E.g:
## extraContainerPorts:
## - name: new_port_name
##   containerPort: 1234
##
extraContainerPorts: []
## @param configuration [string] RabbitMQ Configuration file content: required cluster configuration
## Do not override unless you know what you are doing.
## To add more configuration, use `extraConfiguration` of `advancedConfiguration` instead
##

## RabbitMQ tcp_listen_options parameters
## See : https://www.rabbitmq.com/networking.html for additional information
##
tcpListenOptions:
  ## @param tcpListenOptions.enabled Enable TCP listen options of RabbitMQ
  ##
  enabled: true
  ## @param tcpListenOptions.backlog Maximum size of the unaccepted TCP connections queue
  ##
  backlog: 128
  ## @param tcpListenOptions.nodelay When set to true, deactivates Nagle's algorithm. Default is true. Highly recommended for most users.
  ##
  nodelay: true
  ## tcpListenOptions.linger
  ##
  linger:
    ## @param tcpListenOptions.linger.lingerOn Enable Server socket lingering
    ##
    lingerOn: true
    ## @param tcpListenOptions.linger.timeout Server Socket lingering timeout
    ##
    timeout: 0
  ## @param tcpListenOptions.keepalive When set to true, enables TCP keepalives
  ##
  keepalive: false
configuration: |-
  ## Username and password
  default_user = {{ .Values.auth.username }}
  {{- if and (not .Values.auth.securePassword) .Values.auth.password }}
  default_pass = {{ .Values.auth.password }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.clustering.enabled }}
  ## Clustering
  ##
  cluster_name = {{ default (include "common.names.fullname" .) .Values.clustering.name }}
  cluster_formation.peer_discovery_backend  = rabbit_peer_discovery_k8s
  cluster_formation.k8s.host = kubernetes.default
  cluster_formation.k8s.address_type = {{ .Values.clustering.addressType }}
  {{- $svcName := printf "%s-%s" (include "common.names.fullname" .) (default "headless" .Values.servicenameOverride) }}
  cluster_formation.k8s.service_name = {{ $svcName }}
  cluster_formation.k8s.hostname_suffix = .{{ $svcName }}.{{ include "common.names.namespace" . }}.svc.{{ .Values.clusterDomain }}
  cluster_formation.node_cleanup.interval = 10
  cluster_formation.node_cleanup.only_log_warning = true
  cluster_partition_handling = {{ .Values.clustering.partitionHandling }}
  {{- end }}
  {{ if and .Values.clustering.enabled .Values.loadDefinition.enabled }}
  cluster_formation.target_cluster_size_hint = {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  {{ end }}
  {{- if .Values.loadDefinition.enabled }}
  load_definitions = {{ .Values.loadDefinition.file }}
  {{- end }}
  # queue leader locator
  queue_leader_locator = {{ include "rabbitmq.queueLocator" . }}
  # enable loopback user
  {{- if not (empty .Values.auth.username) }}
  loopback_users.{{ .Values.auth.username }} = {{ .Values.auth.enableLoopbackUser }}
  {{- else}}
  loopback_users.guest = {{ .Values.auth.enableLoopbackUser }}
  {{- end }}
  {{ template "rabbitmq.extraConfiguration" . }}
  {{- if .Values.auth.tls.enabled }}
  ssl_options.verify = {{ .Values.auth.tls.sslOptionsVerify }}
  listeners.ssl.default = {{ .Values.service.ports.amqpTls }}
  ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = {{ .Values.auth.tls.failIfNoPeerCert }}
  ssl_options.cacertfile = /opt/bitnami/rabbitmq/certs/ca_certificate.pem
  ssl_options.certfile = /opt/bitnami/rabbitmq/certs/server_certificate.pem
  ssl_options.keyfile = /opt/bitnami/rabbitmq/certs/server_key.pem
  {{- if .Values.auth.tls.sslOptionsPassword.enabled }}
  ssl_options.password = {{ include "common.secrets.passwords.manage" (dict "secret" .Values.auth.tls.sslOptionsPassword.existingSecret "key" .Values.auth.tls.sslOptionsPassword.key "providedValues" (list "auth.tls.sslOptionsPassword.password") "skipB64enc" true "failOnNew" false "context" $) }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.enabled }}
  auth_backends.1.authn = ldap
  auth_backends.1.authz = {{ ternary "ldap" "internal" .Values.ldap.authorisationEnabled }}
  auth_backends.2 = internal
  {{- $host :=  list }}
  {{- $port :=  ternary 636 389 .Values.ldap.tls.enabled }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.uri }}
  {{- $hostPort := get (urlParse .Values.ldap.uri) "host" }}
  {{- $host = list (index (splitList ":" $hostPort) 0) -}}
  {{- if (contains ":" $hostPort) }}
  {{- $port = index (splitList ":" $hostPort) 1 -}}
  {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- range $index, $server := concat $host .Values.ldap.servers }}
  auth_ldap.servers.{{ add $index 1 }} = {{ $server }}
  {{- end }}
  auth_ldap.port = {{ coalesce .Values.ldap.port $port }}
  {{- if or .Values.ldap.user_dn_pattern .Values.ldap.userDnPattern }}
  auth_ldap.user_dn_pattern = {{ coalesce .Values.ldap.user_dn_pattern .Values.ldap.userDnPattern }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.basedn }}
  auth_ldap.dn_lookup_base = {{ .Values.ldap.basedn }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.uidField }}
  auth_ldap.dn_lookup_attribute = {{ .Values.ldap.uidField }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.binddn }}
  auth_ldap.dn_lookup_bind.user_dn = {{ .Values.ldap.binddn }}
  auth_ldap.dn_lookup_bind.password = {{ required "'ldap.bindpw' is required when 'ldap.binddn' is defined" .Values.ldap.bindpw }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.tls.enabled }}
  auth_ldap.use_ssl = {{ not .Values.ldap.tls.startTls }}
  auth_ldap.use_starttls = {{ .Values.ldap.tls.startTls }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.tls.CAFilename }}
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.cacertfile = {{ .Values.ldap.tls.certificatesMountPath }}/{{ .Values.ldap.tls.CAFilename }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.tls.certFilename }}
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.certfile = {{ .Values.ldap.tls.certificatesMountPath }}/{{ .Values.ldap.tls.certFilename }}
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.keyfile = {{ .Values.ldap.tls.certificatesMountPath }}/{{ required "'ldap.tls.certKeyFilename' is required when 'ldap.tls.certFilename' is defined" .Values.ldap.tls.certKeyFilename }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- if .Values.ldap.tls.skipVerify }}
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.verify = verify_none
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.fail_if_no_peer_cert = false
  {{- else if .Values.ldap.tls.verify }}
  auth_ldap.ssl_options.verify = {{ .Values.ldap.tls.verify }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
  {{- end }}
  ## Prometheus metrics
  ##
  prometheus.tcp.port = {{ .Values.containerPorts.metrics }}
  {{- if .Values.memoryHighWatermark.enabled }}
  ## Memory Threshold

  storageClass: ""

  tag: 4.1.3-debian-12-r17
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  pullSecrets: []
  debug: false

## @section RabbitMQ Configuration
## RabbitMQ cluster name
clusterName: cue-rabbitmq

## Erlang cookie secret
auth:
  existingErlangSecret: ""
  erlangCookie: ""
  username: cue
  password: ""
  existingPasswordSecret: ""

management:
  enabled: true
  plugin: rabbitmq_management
  path: /api
  loadDefinitions:
    enabled: false
    definitions: ""
  service:

    nodePort: ""
    annotations: {}
    labels: {}
  ingress:
    enabled: false
    hostname: rabbitmq.cue.local
    path: /
    annotations: {}
    className: ""
    tls: false
    secrets: []
    extraPaths: []

prometheus:
  enabled: true
  port: 9090
  path: /metrics
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 9090
    annotations:
      prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
      prometheus.io/port: "9090"

    resources: {}
    env: {}

    memory: 1Gi

  selector: {}

replicaCount: 1
autoscaling:

nodeSelector: {}
tolerations: []
affinity:

  enabled: false

    to: []
    ports: []

  runAsUser: 1001
  runAsGroup: 1001
  runAsNonRoot: true

  labels: {}
  clusterIP: ""

  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster

# Based on Bitnami RabbitMQ Helm Chart v16.0.14

## @section Global parameters
## Global Docker image parameters
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullSecrets: []
  defaultStorageClass: ""
  storageClass: ""
  security:
    allowInsecureImages: false
  compatibility:
    openshift:
      adaptSecurityContext: auto

## @section RabbitMQ Image parameters
image:
  registry: docker.io
  repository: bitnami/rabbitmq
  tag: 4.1.3-debian-12-r17
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  pullSecrets: []
  debug: false

## @section RabbitMQ Configuration
## RabbitMQ cluster name
clusterName: cue-rabbitmq

## Erlang cookie secret
auth:
  existingErlangSecret: ""
  erlangCookie: ""
  username: cue
  password: ""
  existingPasswordSecret: ""

## RabbitMQ management UI
management:
  enabled: true
  plugin: rabbitmq_management
  path: /api
  loadDefinitions:
    enabled: false
    definitions: ""
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 15672
    nodePort: ""
    annotations: {}
    labels: {}
  ingress:
    enabled: false
    hostname: rabbitmq.cue.local
    path: /
    annotations: {}
    className: ""
    tls: false
    secrets: []
    extraPaths: []

## Prometheus metrics exporter
prometheus:
  enabled: true
  port: 9090
  path: /metrics
  service:
    type: ClusterIP
    port: 9090
    annotations:
      prometheus.io/scrape: "true"
      prometheus.io/port: "9090"
    labels: {}
  exporter:
    enabled: true
    image:
      registry: docker.io
      repository: bitnami/rabbitmq-exporter
      tag: 0.11.1-debian-12-r10
      pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
      pullSecrets: []
    resources: {}
    env: {}
    extraFlags: ""

## Resource limits
resources:
  limits:
    cpu: 1000m
    memory: 1Gi
  requests:
    cpu: 500m
    memory: 512Mi

## Persistence configuration
persistence:
  enabled: true
  storageClass: ""
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  size: 8Gi
  annotations: {}
  selector: {}
  existingClaim: ""

## Node configuration
replicaCount: 1
autoscaling:
  enabled: false
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 3
  targetCPUUtilizationPercentage: 80

## Pod scheduling
nodeSelector: {}
tolerations: []
affinity:
  podAntiAffinity: soft

## Network policies
networkPolicy:
  enabled: false
  ingress:
    from: []
    ports:
      - port: 5672
      - port: 15672
      - port: 15692
      - port: 25672
      - port: 4369
      - port: 9090
  egress:
    to: []
    ports: []

## Security context
podSecurityContext:
  enabled: true
  fsGroup: 1001
  runAsUser: 1001
  runAsGroup: 1001
  runAsNonRoot: true
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

containerSecurityContext:
  enabled: true
  runAsUser: 1001
  runAsGroup: 1001
  runAsNonRoot: true
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  capabilities:
    drop:
      - ALL
  seccompProfile:
    type: RuntimeDefault

## Service configuration
service:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    amqp: 5672
    dist: 25672
    http: 15672
  annotations: {}
  labels: {}
  clusterIP: ""
  loadBalancerIP: ""
  loadBalancerSourceRanges: []
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster

## Headless service for clustering
headlessService:
  enabled: true
  annotations: {}
  labels: {}

## Extra configuration
extraConfiguration: |-
  loopback_users.guest = false
  default_user = cue
  default_pass = CHANGE_ME
  default_vhost = /
  default_permissions.configure = .*
  default_permissions.read = .*
  default_permissions.write = .*
  log.console.level = info
  log.file.level = info

## Plugins to enable
extraPlugins: []
enabledPlugins:
  - rabbitmq_management
  - rabbitmq_prometheus
  - rabbitmq_peer_discovery_k8s
  - rabbitmq_shovel
  - rabbitmq_shovel_management

sysctls:
  - name: net.core.somaxconn

# Default values for cue.
# This is a YAML-formatted file.
# Declare variables to be passed into your templates.

replicaCount: 1

sealedSecrets:
  enabled: false

image:
  registry: docker.io
  repository: cue
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  # Overrides the image tag whose default is the chart appVersion.
  tag: "latest"

# Global image settings for all services
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services common configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
  env: {}

# List of backend services
backendServices:
  - name: auth-service
    port: 8080
  - name: user-service
    port: 8080
  - name: profile-service
    port: 8080
  - name: discovery-service
    port: 8080
  - name: booking-service
    port: 8080
  - name: payment-service
    port: 8080
  - name: chat-service
    port: 8080
  - name: notification-service
    port: 8080
  - name: review-service
    port: 8080
  - name: support-service
    port: 8080
  - name: analytics-service
    port: 8080
  - name: api-gateway
    port: 8080

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m

# Infrastructure services
postgres:
  imageTag: "15.19"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
  persistence:
    enabled: false
    # existingVolumeName:
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 10Gi

rabbitmq:
  imageTag: "3-management"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m

redis:
  imageTag: "7-alpine"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

jaeger:
  imageTag: "1.47"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 1Gi
      cpu: 500m
    requests:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 250m

# Secret values (to be set by the user, preferably via --set-file or --set-string)
# RAW secrets (no base64 required)
# Example: echo -n "your-value" | base64
secret:
  # PostgreSQL credentials
  POSTGRES_USER: postgres
  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
  POSTGRES_DB: cue_db

  # RabbitMQ credentials
  RABBITMQ_USER: admin
  RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: secret

  # Redis password
  REDIS_PASSWORD: secret

  # Stripe API key for payments
  STRIPE_SECRET_KEY: sk_test_421ffVAem5k5Ea8 # placeholder

  # JWT signing key for authentication tokens
  JWT_SIGNING_KEY: supersecretjwtskieforlocal # placeholder

  # Auth Service specific secrets
  JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES: "15"
  JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_DAYS: "7"

  # Database connection strings
  AUTH_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Auth Service DB connection string
  USER_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # User Service DB connection string
  BOOKING_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Booking Service DB connection string
  PAYMENT_DB_CONNECTION: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret
  # Payment Service DB connection string
  # Connection string for AuthService (used by Entity Framework Core)
  ConnectionStrings__CueDatabase: Host=loveagain-cue-postgres-service;Port=5432;Database=cue_db;Username=postgres;Password=secret

  # Email service credentials (if using external email provider)
  EMAIL_API_KEY: c2vjcmV0 # placeholder
  EMAIL_FROM_ADDRESS: cue@mailcompany.com

  # Redis connection strings
  REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING: redis://redis:6379

# Example of how to generate base64 values:
# Linux/macOS:  echo -n "your-value" | base64
# Windows PS:   [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("your-value"))

# Ingress configuration

  enabled: false
  className: ""
  annotations: {}
    # kubernetes.io/ingress.class: nginx

  hosts:
    - host: chart-example.local

# Local deployment values for cue-platform Helm chart
# For deployment on a local k3s/minikube cluster

# Global image settings
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# PostgreSQL configuration
postgres:
  imageTag: 15-3.4
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

    enabled: true

# RabbitMQ configuration
rabbitmq:

    limits:

      cpu: 250m
    requests:

      cpu: 100m

# Redis configuration
redis:

  resources:

      cpu: 100m
    requests:

  resources:

      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 256Mi

secret:
  # PostgreSQL credentials

  POSTGRES_PASSWORD: localsecret
  POSTGRES_DB: cue_db

  # RabbitMQ credentials

  RABBITMQ_PASSWORD: localsecret

  # Redis password

  REDIS_CONNECTION_STRING: redis://redis:6379

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-rabbitmq
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.rabbitmq.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:

        app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq

      containers:
        - name: rabbitmq
          image: "rabbitmq:{{ .Values.rabbitmq.imageTag | default "3-management" }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.global.imagePullPolicy | default "IfNotPresent" }}
          ports:
            - name: amqp
              containerPort: 5672
              protocol: TCP
            - name: http

            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER
              valueFrom:

                  key: RABBITMQ_USER
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-backend-secret

            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST

                - check_running

            periodSeconds: 10

            exec:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-rabbitmq
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.rabbitmq.replicaCount }}
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 6 }}
      app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 8 }}
        app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: rabbitmq
          image: "rabbitmq:{{ .Values.rabbitmq.imageTag | default "3-management" }}"
          imagePullPolicy: {{ .Values.global.imagePullPolicy | default "IfNotPresent" }}
          ports:
            - name: amqp
              containerPort: 5672
              protocol: TCP
            - name: http
              containerPort: 15672
              protocol: TCP
          env:
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-backend-secret
                  key: RABBITMQ_USER
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-backend-secret
                  key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST
              value: "/"
          livenessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - rabbitmq-diagnostics
                - check_running
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - rabbitmq-diagnostics
                - check_local_alarms
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            {{- toYaml .Values.rabbitmq.resources | nindent 12 }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ include "cue.fullname" . }}-rabbitmq-service
  labels:
    {{- include "cue.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
spec:
  type: {{ .Values.service.type | default "ClusterIP" }}
  ports:
    - port: 5672
      targetPort: 5672
      protocol: TCP
      name: amqp
    - port: 15672
      targetPort: 15672
      protocol: TCP
      name: http
  selector:
    {{- include "cue.selectorLabels" . | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq

  name: cue-cue-rabbitmq

    helm.sh/chart: cue-0.1.0
    app.kubernetes.io/name: cue
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: cue
    app.kubernetes.io/version: 1.0.0

  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: cue
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: cue
      app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq

    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: cue
        app.kubernetes.io/instance: cue
        app.kubernetes.io/name: rabbitmq
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: rabbitmq
          image: "rabbitmq:3-management"
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          ports:
            - name: amqp
              containerPort: 5672
              protocol: TCP
            - name: http
              containerPort: 15672
              protocol: TCP
          env:
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: cue-cue-backend-secret
                  key: RABBITMQ_USER
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: cue-cue-backend-secret
                  key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
            - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_VHOST
              value: "/"
          livenessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - rabbitmq-diagnostics
                - check_running
            initialDelaySeconds: 60
            periodSeconds: 10
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command:
                - rabbitmq-diagnostics
                - check_local_alarms
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            limits:
              cpu: 250m
              memory: 256Mi
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
          volumeMounts:
            - name: rabbitmq-data
              mountPath: /var/lib/rabbitmq
      volumes:
        - name: rabbitmq-data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: cue-cue-rabbitmq-pvc
---

content.text:
**Yes, exactly!** The backend services and RabbitMQ both use the **same secret** `cue-cue-backend-secret`. Here's how it works:

## 🔐 Secret Structure

The secret `cue-cue-backend-secret` contains **all** configuration as base64-encoded keys:

| Key | Value (decoded) | Used By |
|-----|-----------------|---------|
| `RABBITMQ_USER` | `admin` | Backend services + RabbitMQ |
| `RABBITMQ_PASSWORD` | `localsecret` | Backend services + RabbitMQ |
| `RABBITMQ_CONNECTION_STRING` | `amqp://admin:localsecret@rabbitmq:5672` | Backend services |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | `admin` | Backend services |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `localsecret` | Backend services |
| ... | ... | ... |

## 📦 How Services Consume It

### Backend Services (in `backend-service.yaml`):
```yaml
envFrom:
  - configMapRef:
      name: cue-cue-backend-config
  - secretRef:
      name: cue-cue-backend-secret  # ← Loads ALL keys as env vars
```

### RabbitMQ Deployment (in `rabbitmq-deployment.yaml`):
```yaml
env:
  - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: cue-cue-backend-secret
        key: RABBITMQ_USER
  - name: RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: cue-cue-backend-secret
        key: RABBITMQ_PASSWORD
```

## ✅ Key Points

1. **Single Source of Truth**: Both RabbitMQ and backend services get credentials from the same secret
2. **Backend services** get `RABBITMQ_CONNECTION_STRING` pre-built for easy connection
3. **RabbitMQ** gets `RABBITMQ_USER`/`RABBITMQ_PASSWORD` to create the default user on startup
4. **Consistency**: When you update values in `values.yaml` or `values-local.yaml`, both get the same credentials automatically

## 🔗 Connection Flow

```
Backend Service → reads RABBITMQ_CONNECTION_STRING from secret
                → connects to: amqp://admin:localsecret@rabbitmq:5672
                → resolves to: cue-cue-rabbitmq-service:5672 (ClusterIP)

RabbitMQ → reads RABBITMQ_USER/RABBITMQ_PASSWORD from secret   → creates default user "admin" with password "localsecret"
```

This ensures perfect synchronization - no credential drift possible!

# Local deployment values for cue-platform Helm chart
# For deployment on a local k3s/minikube cluster

# Global image settings
global:
  imageRegistry: ""
  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent

# Backend services configuration
backend:
  replicaCount: 1
  imageTag: latest
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# Frontend configuration
frontend:
  imageTag: latest
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m

# PostgreSQL configuration
postgres:
  imageTag: 15-3.4
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
    size: 5Gi

# RabbitMQ configuration
rabbitmq:
  imageTag: "3-management"
  replicaCount: 1
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 256Mi
      cpu: 250m
    requests:
      memory: 128Mi
      cpu: 100m
  # Additional configuration
  vhost: "/"
  management:
    enabled: true
    plugin: rabbitmq_management
  # Persistence (optional - enable if needed)
  persistence:
    enabled: true
    storageClass: ""
    accessMode: ReadWriteOnce

  resources:

content.text:
The ingress is already configured in `values-local.yaml` (enabled: true), but Rancher Desktop uses **Traefik** as the default ingress controller, not nginx. Here are your options to expose the frontend from Windows:

## Option 1: Port-Forward (Simplest - Works Immediately)
```bash
# Run in a terminal - keeps running
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-frontend-service 3000:3000
# Access: http://localhost:3000
```

## Option 2: Change Service to NodePort (Persistent)
Change the service type in `values-local.yaml`:

```yaml
# Add this to values-local.yaml under the global section or override:
service:
  type: NodePort
```

Then the frontend will be accessible at `http://localhost:<nodeport>` (typically 30000-32767 range).

## Option 3: Use Traefik Ingress (Already Configured)
Rancher Desktop includes Traefik. Update the ingress class:

```yaml
# In values-local.yaml, change:
ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: "traefik"  # Not "nginx"
  annotations:
    traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.entrypoints: web
  hosts:
    - host: cue.local
```

Then add to Windows hosts file (`C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts`):
```
127.0.0.1 cue.local
```

## Option 4: Use kubectl proxy (Alternative)
```bash
kubectl proxy --port=8001
# Access: http://localhost:8001/api/v1/namespaces/cue-platform/services/cue-cue-frontend-service:3000/proxy/
```

content.text:
The services are behind an **API Gateway**. The frontend (port 3000) talks to the gateway. Here's how to access Swagger:

## Option 1: Port-forward directly to Auth Service (Direct Access)
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/auth-service 8080:8080
# Swagger: http://localhost:8080/swagger
# Or: http://localhost:8080/swagger/index.html
```

## Option 2: Port-forward to API Gateway (Routes through gateway)
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-api-gateway 8080:8080
# Auth Swagger via gateway: http://localhost:8080/api/auth/swagger
# Or check gateway's Swagger aggregation: http://localhost:8080/swagger
```

## Option 3: Use the Ingress (If running with Traefik)
If you have ingress working with `cue.local`:
```
http://cue.local/api/auth/swagger
```

---

## Quick Commands for Multiple Services:

```bash
# Frontendkubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-frontend-service 3000:3000 &

# Auth Service Swagger (direct)
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/auth-service 8081:8080 &

# API Gateway (for all APIs)
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-api-gateway 8080:8080 &

# RabbitMQ Management
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-rabbitmq-service 15672:15672 &
```

**Then access:**
- Frontend: `http://localhost:3000`
- Auth Swagger: `http://localhost:8081/swagger`
- API Gateway: `http://localhost:8080`

---

## Note on Swagger Path
The exact Swagger path depends on your .NET service configuration. Common paths:
- `http://localhost:8081/swagger`
- `http://localhost:8081/swagger/index.html`
- `http://localhost:8081/api/swagger`

Check your `Program.cs` or `Startup.cs` for:
```csharp
app.UseSwagger();
app.UseSwaggerUI(c => c.SwaggerEndpoint("/swagger/v1/swagger.json", "Auth API v1"));
```

The path is typically `/swagger` for the UI and `/swagger/v1/swagger.json` for the JSON spec.

FROM node:20-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files
COPY package*.json ./

# Install dependencies
RUN npm ci

# Copy source
COPY . .

# Build the app
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine

WORKDIR /app

# Install a lightweight HTTP server to serve the static build
RUN npm install -g serve

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Health check
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=3s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000', (r) => {if (r.statusCode !== 200) throw new Error(r.statusCode)})"

# Start the application
CMD ["serve", "-s", "dist", "-l", "3000"]

## 🔧 Quick Access: Port-forward Directly to Services

While developing, access Swagger directly:

### 1. Auth Service Swagger
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/auth-service 8081:8080
# Access: http://localhost:8081/swagger
```

### 2. User Service Swagger
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/user-service 8082:8080  
# Access: http://localhost:8082/swagger
```

### 3. API Gateway (aggregated routes)
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-api-gateway 8083:8080
# Access: http://localhost:8083/swagger (if gateway aggregates)
# Or specific service: http://localhost:8083/api/auth/swagger
```

### 4. Frontend (still need this for UI)
```bash
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-frontend-service 3000:3000 &
```

## 🏗️ Alternative: Configure Frontend Proxy (No Code Changes)

If you want the frontend at localhost:3000 to proxy API calls:

### Update `vite.config.ts`:
```typescript
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import tailwindcss from '@tailwindcss/vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    react(),
    tailwindcss(),
  ],
  server: {
    proxy: {
      '/api': {
        target: 'http://localhost:8080',
        changeOrigin: true,
        secure: false,
        ws: true
      }
    }
  }
})
```

Then:
```bash
# Terminal 1: Frontend
cd /e/Projects/Github/one-brain/LoveAgain/frontend
npm run dev  # Will be at http://localhost:5173 (Vite dev server)

# Terminal 2: API Gateway
kubectl port-forward -n cue-platform svc/cue-cue-api-gateway 8080:8080
```

Now frontend API calls to `/api/*` will proxy to your Kubernetes services.

## 📝 Recommendation

For development:
1. Use **Vite dev server** (`npm run dev`) for hot reload
2. Use **port-forward** for backend services
3. Configure **Vite proxy** to route `/api` to gateway

This gives you:
- Frontend: `http://localhost:5173` (hot reload)
- API: Proxied to Kubernetes via `localhost:5173/api/*`
- Swagger: Access via `localhost:5173/api/auth/swagger`
